mission.earthObserver.title: Earth Observer
mission.earthObserver.brief: Put an imaging satellite into low Earth orbit and deliver enough data to meet the science team's requirements.
agency.borealis.name: Borealis Federation
agency.borealis.description: Large budget and the full range of launchers. Strong in software and electronics, weak in metallurgy.
agency.monsoon.name: Monsoon Union
agency.monsoon.description: Small budget, cheap launchers and strong software. No heavy launcher.
agency.kestrel.name: Kestrel Republic
agency.kestrel.description: Cheap launchers and strong heavy industry, weaker electronics and optics. Sanctions block the large camera and antenna, so they have to be developed at home.
agency.meridia.name: Meridia Concord
agency.meridia.description: Average budget, very strong optics. Careful development takes longer.

ui.waitHint: Waiting makes new modules cheaper, but the deadline gets closer and data from a late launch is worth less.

mission.disasterResponse.title: Disaster Response
mission.disasterResponse.brief: A flood has hit the delta. Rescuers need sharp, fresh images fast: a low orbit, a short mission, and data that loses value every turn.
mission.iceWatch.title: Ice Watch
mission.iceWatch.brief: Map polar ice over a long mission. Resolution matters less than volume, but the orbits are long and partly in shadow.
mission.bigEye.title: Big Eye
mission.bigEye.brief: Scientists want images sharper than any catalogue camera can take. Build your own mirror, and pray it is ground right.
mission.guest.title: The Guest
mission.guest.brief: An asteroid passes close to Earth, as Apophis will in April 2029. There are only a few launch windows: collect as much data as you can.
mission.selene.title: Selene
mission.selene.brief: Map the Moon from a low lunar orbit. Getting there costs a lot of delta-v, and passes over the relay are short.
scenario.livingPlanet.title: Living Planet
scenario.livingPlanet.brief: A five-window Earth observation programme. The baseline campaign.
scenario.disaster.title: Disaster Response
scenario.disaster.brief: Three short windows, data that goes stale fast.
scenario.iceWatch.title: Ice Watch
scenario.iceWatch.brief: Long missions, lots of data, long shadows.
scenario.bigEye.title: Big Eye
scenario.bigEye.brief: Only a custom mirror is sharp enough. Hubble-style defects included.
scenario.guest.title: The Guest
scenario.guest.brief: Two windows while an asteroid passes Earth. No target: grab all you can.
scenario.selene.title: Selene
scenario.selene.brief: A lunar mapping race where delta-v and short relay passes are the bottleneck.
research.testStand: Test stand: defect risk of own development ×0.7
research.earlyAccess: Supplier contracts: new modules appear 2 turns earlier for you
research.scouting: Scouting probe: learn the real mission conditions without a launch
research.series: Series production: relaunching the same design refunds 15%
ui.research.title: Research ({pts} points)
ui.research.hint: Points come from delivered data and from windows you skip. Research does not use up turn actions.
factory.line.alloy: Al-Li alloy → tanks and combustion chamber
factory.hint.alloy.bayer: Caustic digestion drops iron oxide out as red mud.
factory.hint.alloy.sinter: Binds silica before digestion; slower and hotter.
factory.hint.alloy.var: Boils off volatile copper and gases.
factory.hint.alloy.flux: Chlorine flux strips copper and some silica.
factory.hint.semi.siemens: Trichlorosilane distillation removes boron and iron.
factory.hint.semi.fz: Sweeps oxygen and boron out of the crystal.
factory.hint.cells.lime: Precipitates magnesium out of the brine.
factory.hint.cells.recryst: Grows clean cathode crystals; removes sodium.
factory.line.rf: Copper and rare earths → RF amplifier
factory.hint.rf.solvent: Separates thorium from the rare earths.
factory.hint.rf.ofhc: Copper cast under vacuum: no oxygen.
factory.hint.rf.zone: Slow sweep that removes sulfur and oxygen.
factory.hint.glass.magnetic: Pulls iron-bearing grains out of the sand.
factory.hint.glass.fine: Holds the melt hot so bubbles rise out.
factory.hint.glass.anneal: Weeks of controlled cooling relieve internal stress.
factory.hint.glass.polish: Figure the mirror; hides nothing inside the glass.
factory.hint.glass.hip: Squeezes out bubbles and stress; slow.
ui.factory.title: Factory
ui.factory.hint: Make a module yourself: pick raw material, then one step at each stage. Steps that cure the material's flaws raise quality; uncured flaws lower it. Cheap domestic ore with the right route matches imported quality.
ui.factory.busy: A workshop on this route is busy.
campaign.lostInFlight: The spacecraft was lost during the flight and never reached its orbit.
mission.stationResupply.title: Station Resupply
mission.stationResupply.brief: The station is running low. Pick one container (water, food, spare parts or an experiment), reach the station orbit and keep the spacecraft alive through the approach. Three containers of the same thing are worth less than a mix.
scenario.lifeline.title: Lifeline
scenario.lifeline.brief: Three short windows to keep a space station supplied. Coordinate what each agency brings.
ui.campaign.actionsFull: You have used all {n} commands this report can carry. Send the report: the remaining orbits run on autopilot.
trl.failure.engine: The {module} (TRL {trl}, {chancePercent}% risk) underperformed after launch: {lossPercent}% of its thrust lost, the way Mars Observer's untested propulsion line failed.
trl.failure.solar: The {module} (TRL {trl}, {chancePercent}% risk) did not fully deploy: {lossPercent}% of power lost, like Skylab's torn array.
trl.failure.battery: The {module} (TRL {trl}, {chancePercent}% risk) degraded early: {lossPercent}% of capacity lost, like the battery that ended Mars Global Surveyor.
trl.failure.antenna: The {module} (TRL {trl}, {chancePercent}% risk) jammed half-open: {lossPercent}% of the link lost, like Galileo's high-gain antenna.
trl.failure.instrument: The {module} (TRL {trl}, {chancePercent}% risk) came out of focus: {lossPercent}% of image quality lost, like Hubble's first mirror.
ui.trl.title: Technology readiness (TRL)
ui.trl.hint: New technology is not more expensive, it is less proven. Every successful flight and every ground test makes it one level more mature for your agency.
scenario.living-planet.analog: Landsat 9: NASA and USGS launched Landsat 9 in 2021 to continue a 50-year record of Earth's land surface.
scenario.disaster.analog: Sentinel-1 and the Copernicus emergency service: Radar satellites map floods within hours for rescuers; stale images lose value fast.
scenario.ice-watch.analog: ICESat-2: Launched in 2018, its laser altimeter measures polar ice height to a few centimetres, orbit after orbit.
scenario.big-eye.analog: Hubble Space Telescope: Launched in 1990 with a mirror ground 2 microns too flat; astronauts installed corrective optics in 1993.
scenario.guest.analog: OSIRIS-APEX: The OSIRIS-REx spacecraft was redirected to meet asteroid Apophis after its 2029 close pass by Earth.
scenario.selene.analog: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter: Mapping the Moon from a 50 km orbit since 2009; most of its data goes home during short relay passes.
scenario.lifeline.analog: Cygnus and Dragon resupply flights: Commercial cargo ships bring water, food, spare parts and experiments to the ISS several times a year.
ui.brief.title: Briefing from the mission director
ui.brief.unknown: We have never flown this mission. The real conditions are unknown until our first launch (or a scouting probe), so treat the first flight as reconnaissance.
ui.brief.known: We know the real conditions now: plan for them, not for the brochure numbers.
ui.brief.window: Window {n} of {total}: {turns} turn(s) to launch. Every turn you wait makes the data a little less valuable.
ui.brief.missed: We skipped the last window. Skip another one and the funding will be cut hard.
ui.brief.upcoming: Suppliers promise {n} new module(s) soon. Waiting may pay off — or may cost us the window.
ui.brief.risk: Some modules in our design are not flight-proven yet (see TRL). A ground test or two would lower the risk.
ui.brief.lastResult: Last window we got {value} of the {optimal} the best available design would have given ({percent}%).
ui.campaign.optimal: Best available design would have given {optimal} ({percent}% achieved).
mission.marsRelay.title: Red Planet Mapper
mission.marsRelay.brief: Map Mars from a low orbit. Getting there takes a lot of delta-v, and the data trickles home over short relay passes.
scenario.redPlanet.title: Red Planet
scenario.redPlanet.brief: Launch windows to Mars open only every 26 months. Between windows you can only build, test and research. Miss one and you wait.
scenario.red-planet.analog: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter: launched in the 2005 window, it has mapped Mars and relayed rover data home since 2006.
ui.brief.gap: After this window the next launch opportunity is {gap} turns away. Use that time for factory batches, tests and research.
scenario.goldRush.title: Gold Rush
scenario.goldRush.brief: Commercial imagery race: the first agency to bank 550 M$ wins. Every image sold makes the next one cheaper.
scenario.gold-rush.analog: Planet Labs and Maxar: commercial constellations where whoever photographs first gets paid, and stale imagery is worth little.
scenario.firstLight.title: First Light
scenario.firstLight.brief: A race: the first agency whose single mission delivers a breakthrough (contribution 80+) wins outright.
scenario.first-light.analog: The race for the first sharp images of distant galaxies, from Hubble's fixed optics to the James Webb Space Telescope.
ui.campaign.winnerProgram: {agency} wins: the biggest contribution to the science programme.
ui.campaign.winnerCommercial: {agency} wins the commercial race with {funds} M$.
ui.campaign.winnerRace: {agency} wins the race with a breakthrough mission.
ui.brief.victoryCommercial: Victory: the first agency to bank {target} M$. Each image sold lowers the price of the next.
ui.brief.victoryRace: Victory: the first single mission with a contribution of {target} or more.

ui.ground.hint: Every own ground station makes each contact pass {percent}% longer (now {pass} s per orbit), so more data gets home.
ui.ground.build: Build a ground station ({cost} M$, 1 action)
mission.cubesat101.title: CubeSat 101
mission.cubesat101.brief: Your first small Earth-imaging satellite: a low orbit, a modest camera, a short mission. Learn the margins before the big programmes.
scenario.cubesat101.title: CubeSat 101 (tutorial)
scenario.cubesat101.brief: Two short windows to learn the ropes. The mission director explains every red margin.
scenario.cubesat-101.analog: NASA's CubeSat Launch Initiative: student teams fly 10 cm satellites to learn mission design on a small budget.
ui.advice.title: Director's notes on your design:
ui.advice.dv: Delta-v is short: add fuel, or pick a more efficient engine (higher Isp).
ui.advice.energy: The battery will not survive the night side: a bigger battery, bigger panels, or fewer power-hungry modules.
ui.advice.link: The camera takes more data than the antenna can send home per pass: a faster antenna or a slower camera.
ui.advice.science: The images are not sharp enough: a bigger aperture, or fly lower.
ui.advice.mass: Too heavy for the launcher: pick a bigger launcher or lighter modules.
ui.advice.budget: Over budget: cheaper modules or a smaller launcher.
ui.advice.allGood: Every margin is green. Launch now, or wait for better modules if the window allows.
mission.colony.title: Colony Lifeline
mission.colony.brief: The Mars base is running out of food and spare parts, and the next launch window is months away. Reach the depot orbit and keep the ship alive through the approach.
scenario.colony.title: Colony in Trouble
scenario.colony.brief: A Mars base needs supplies before winter. Windows open rarely; between them you can only build and test. Fill the programme or the colony freezes.
scenario.colony.analog: NASA's Mars Design Reference Architecture: cargo is pre-positioned one launch window ahead of the crew, because the next chance is 26 months away.
ui.campaign.colonyLost: The colony did not get enough supplies before winter.
ui.campaign.colonySaved: The colony is supplied for the winter.
